issues.description: Three chain steps (coding-agent, verification-gate, project-state-updater) were executed in-process but never invoked via the Skill tool. The substance of each ran (HTML/Worker authoring; Playwright + wrangler dev evidence captured; project-state.md edit committed) and the expected artifacts exist, but the Skill-tool announce-and-load contract that Guard 5 requires for in-process chain execution was skipped. failure-postmortem itself IS being invoked via the Skill tool — confirming the discipline is enforceable, just inconsistently applied.
issues.detected_by: Transcript inspection: only `workflow-orchestrator` and `failure-postmortem` appear as Skill tool invocations in this run's transcript. Guard 5 explicitly: 'When executing a chain step in-process, the orchestrator MUST: 1. Invoke the skill via the Skill tool. Reading the file with Read does not count.'

issues.description: TodoWrite items were created (#1 Phase 1 … #6 Phase 6) but as orchestrator-level phase tasks, NOT as expansions of each downstream skill's Completion Checklist. Each skill's SKILL.md says 'expand into TodoWrite items at start' — and since each skill was executed in-process rather than dispatched, that expansion never happened. This is the in-process counterpart of W1: even when running in-process, the skill's checklist should still be the TodoWrite source of truth.
issues.detected_by: TaskList contents are 6 phase-level items, not skill-checklist-level items. No per-skill checklist expansion seen in transcript.

suggested_follow_up: When `workflow-orchestrator` runs chain steps in-process for tightly-scoped tasks (no formal issue/contract), enforce Guard 5 explicitly by invoking each step's Skill tool before/around the in-process work — even if the orchestrator believes the step is trivial. Two W1 occurrences in one run (coding-agent + verification-gate + project-state-updater not Skill-invoked) is the pattern; the work was substantively correct but the announce-string + checklist-expansion contract leaked.
